newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BellSouth cuts overseas calls from NZ.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth cuts overseas calls from NZ.

text.p: Mobile telephone company BellSouth said on Tuesday it was cutting international call charges from New Zealand by between 20 and 50 percent from today.
The price cuts mean that BellSouth mobile telephone customers would pay no more than the standard international call rates offered by Telecom to its landline business customers.
Mobile phone customers generally pay a cellular airtime charge on top of normal international call rates.
BellSouth managing director Larry Carter said the price cuts were by 20 percent on average but for some calls the reduction would be as much as 50 percent.
He said the cuts were the most significant in a range of recent price initiatives by the company.
The cuts to international call rates were a direct result of a multi-million dollar interconnection agreement BellSouth reached with Clear Communications in early August, he said.

Under that agreement, all international calls, and most national calls originated on the BellSouth network are carried by Clear, at a lower cost than had previously been offered to BellSouth by Telecom.
"We said in August that we wanted to pass on savings to our customers. This announcement makes good on that promise," Carter said.
The companies did not detail their interconnection agreement further and denied speculation at the time of a closer working relationship or merger.
Competitive pressure in the telephone market has seen $5 weekend deals for domestic calls offered by both Telecom and Clear in September.
